newsitem.title: USA: UPS CEO says strike talks at an impasse.
newsitem.headline: UPS CEO says strike talks at an impasse.

text.p: United Parcel Service Chief Executive Officer James Kelly said Wednesday that talks with the Teamsters union to end a 10-day-old strike were at an impasse.
"I would characterize them as being at an impasse," he told Cable News Network when asked to characterize the negotiations.

"We reached impasse with the Teamsters two contracts ago," he said. "The Teamsters, at that point, sent out the ballot to our people to vote on, and they voted yes, and they kept working and they didn't lose any paychecks and our business kept on going. And that's what we believe should happen this time."

An ABC News Nightline poll released late Tuesday showed 40 percent of Americans back the union in its fight to win more higher-paying, full-time jobs for the 185,000 Teamsters who walked off their jobs last week.
UPS received only 30 percent support in the survey of 506 adults conducted Monday. The remaining 30 percent said they were neutral.
Kelly, commenting on the poll, told CNN, "I don't know if I can convince Americans. What I'm trying to do is convince UPS people."
